function.description: Generates a comprehensive report based on user activity data within a specified time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier for the user.

start_date.description: The start date for the report period in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the report period, inclusive, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_inactive.description: Flag to determine if inactive users should be included in the report.

report_format.description: The format in which the report will be generated.

**Ionisation methods – a quick guide** | Ionisation technique | Typical application | Key advantages | Common limitations | |----------------------|---------------------|----------------|--------------------| | **Electron Impact (EI)** | Gas‑phase mass spectrometry (GC‑MS) | • Simple, robust;
• Produces reproducible fragmentation patterns;
• Good for volatile, thermally stable compounds | • Requires high vacuum;
• Not suitable for large, labile molecules | | **Chemical Ionisation (CI)** | GC‑MS, some LC‑MS | • Softer than EI → less fragmentation;
• Useful for polar, thermally labile analytes | • Still needs GC‑compatible compounds;
• Lower sensitivity for some species | | **Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionisation (APCI)** | LC‑MS, especially for non‑polar to moderately polar analytes | • Operates at atmospheric pressure → minimal sample prep;
• Good for small molecules, drugs, metabolites | • Less effective for highly polar or large biomolecules | | **Electrospray Ionisation (ESI)** | LC‑MS, proteomics, metabolomics | • Very soft → preserves intact ions;
• Handles large biomolecules (proteins, peptides, nucleic acids);
• Amenable to high‑throughput workflows | • Requires aqueous or polar solvents;
• Suppression effects in complex matrices | | **Matrix‑Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation (MALDI)** | Proteomics, polymers, large biomolecules | • Rapid analysis;
• Minimal sample prep;
• Handles very large molecules (up to >1 MDa) | • Requires matrix selection;
• Limited quantitative accuracy compared to ESI | | **Photoionisation (PI)** | GC‑MS, LC‑MS | • Non‑destructive, soft ionisation;
• Useful for UV‑absorbing compounds | • Requires UV‑active analytes;
• Lower sensitivity for non‑UV‑absorbing species | | **Laser Ablation Ionisation (LAI)** | Solid samples, environmental analysis | • Direct sampling of solids;
• Minimal sample prep | • Requires specialized equipment;
• Limited to certain matrices | | **Field‑Ionisation (FII)** | High‑resolution MS, small molecules | • Extremely soft;
• Produces singly charged ions | • Requires high vacuum;
• Limited throughput | ### Choosing the “best” method 1. **Sample type & matrix** * **Small, volatile organic compounds** → EI or CI (GC‑MS). * **Large biomolecules (proteins, peptides)** → ESI or MALDI (LC‑MS). * **Solid or environmental samples** → LAI or FII. 2. **Desired information** * **Structural elucidation** → EI (rich fragmentation). * **Molecular weight determination** → ESI/MALDI (soft, intact ions). * **Quantitation in complex matrices** → ESI with internal standards. 3. **Instrument availability & expertise** * Many labs have LC‑MS with ESI/APCI; GC‑MS with EI/CI is common. * MALDI requires a MALDI‑TOF instrument and matrix handling skills. 4. **Sensitivity & dynamic range** * ESI generally offers higher sensitivity for polar analytes. * MALDI can handle high‑mass analytes but may suffer from ion suppression. 5. **Speed & throughput** * ESI and APCI are compatible with fast LC gradients. * MALDI can analyze many spots quickly but each spot is a single sample. --- #### Bottom line - **For routine metabolomics or proteomics**: **ESI** (often coupled with LC‑MS/MS) is usually the best choice because it’s soft, versatile, and compatible with high‑throughput workflows. - **For small, volatile compounds**: **EI** (GC‑MS) remains the gold standard. - **For very large biomolecules or polymers**: **MALDI** is often preferred. If you have a specific analyte class or analytical goal in mind, let me know and I can narrow down the recommendation further!
